releases.body:
The free quota is ledged per project id and egress together — measured 2026-10-26: from an exit answering 429 to the genuine CLI under one project id, the same CLI under a brand-new project id answered 200, and a random 40-hex id in this package's own shape answered 200 from a spent exit, twice. The old default `global` is the project id every freeriding plugin user's traffic carries, so its buckets on popular exits arrive pre-burned — which is how a freshly rotated exit once answered 429 twenty-one seconds after first use.

- A request whose host names a project — by `x-opencode-project` or with a git project magpie hands over — keeps that name. A request whose host does not gets a git-hash-shaped id of its own per request (`randomProjectID`): a ledger no other traffic shares, wherever the request lands.
- The gate probes the same way: `tools-smoke.mjs` asks with a fresh project id per probe, or it would report a wording refusal where the truth is a spent `global` bucket.
- Both READMEs and MAINTAINING.md state the pair-keyed ledger and the sharing trap, with the measurements.
- node --test 799 pass (the 8 capture tests want Bun).

The 2.1.4 prompt commands the model to use `execute`, and the official set rides in the tools array because the gates read it — so a model that believes its prompt opened the session by calling `execute` to an unknown-tool error, then the catalog's `shell` to another, before finding the `clint_` names on the third call (measured 2026-10-25 on DeepSeek Harness, twice per session).

- The official prompt is now followed by a `<system-reminder>` — the prompt's own convention for harness instruction — stating that Code Mode is not active here, that the built-ins are not implemented, and naming the `clint_` tools this host actually runs, enumerated per request from the renaming's own output. A host that declared no tools is told so outright.
- The tier does not check the prompt byte for byte — the skills listing was removed in 0.5.5 and the whole 2.1.4 text swapped in 0.5.7, both answered — and this one was verified live too: the full shaping path with the note answered 200 from a live exit under Bun.
- Tests pin the note: names enumerated from the body's `clint_` entries, the no-tools branch, the note sitting between the official prompt and the host's own instructions, and an already-shaped body left untouched.
- node --test 799 pass (the 8 capture tests want Bun).

The free tier retired the 1.x lane on 2026-10-25, and it fingerprints the TLS handshake besides. Both were measured from a live exit with the minute held equal: the 1.19.3 shape answered 429 Free usage limit where the 2.x shape answered 200, and the genuine request replayed byte for byte answered 200 under Bun's ClientHello and 429 under Node's — the same disguised refusal an exhausted quota returns. A DeepSeek Harness session died mid-afternoon exactly at the 1.x default; no IP, session or wording recovers a retired lane.

- Every shaped request now leaves as the 2.x generation, whatever the host's tools declare. A host declaring `bash` used to travel the 1.x lane and be refused for a lane it never chose; the clint_ renaming already keeps its `bash` from colliding with the official set's `shell`.
- The 2.x assets are the real 2.1.4 capture: a new system prompt (the 2.1 line rewrote the prose, so `opencode-prompt-v2.txt` is its own file with placeholders for model, date and environment), and the 12-tool set — `execute` joins, `patch` has left. The 2.x User-Agent moves to `opencode/latest/2.1.4/cli`. The raw request the assets were read from is kept as `genuine-2.1.4-request.json`, and `mini-capture.mjs` is the harness that took it (the `capture.mjs` trick driving the desktop CLI).
- The requests must leave from a Bun runtime, as the official clients do — magpie runs its plugins under the Bun it ships, which is what this package rides; probing from Node is refused no matter how genuine the body. MAINTAINING.md now states both gates outright, with the measurements.
- End-to-end on a live exit under Bun: the full shaping path (host tool under `clint_`, the 2.1.4 prompt and tool set, the 2.1.4 User-Agent, the 32000 ceiling) answered 200.
- node --test 798 pass (the 8 capture tests want Bun).

Every request now leaves as its own session: a fresh OpenCode-shaped `ses_` id is minted per request, and none of the host's session signals is read. The tier keeps what it thinks of traffic against the session — a request arriving as a session it has never seen carries none of that ledger.

- The mint's timestamp is the current moment, always inside the window the tier accepts. That window is load-bearing: the tier decodes the embedded timestamp and answers an id dated far from now with the same 429 a genuinely exhausted quota returns (measured by opencode2api on 2026-10-25 — hash-derived timestamps landing in 1970 made healthy egresses look blocked, its 9533101). `opencodeID` has always stamped `Date.now()`, so this package's ids were never out of window; MAINTAINING.md now states the rule outright: never write a hash into the time field.
- `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_SESSION_AFFINITY=1` restores one session per conversation — the host's OpenCode-shaped id passed through, or one derived from the host's session identifiers and remembered across turns. Read per request, so the host honours it from its next request without a reload.
- Both READMEs, the env table and `.env.example` describe the new default and the knob; `session.test.mjs` pins rotation (two requests are two ids, both current-timestamped, even an official id is not kept) and the knob restoring the ladder.
- Honest limit, stated in the docs too: the exhausted-quota 429 is recorded per egress. Rotation guarantees no request answers for a session's history; it does not move an IP's quota.
- node --test 798 pass (the 8 capture tests want Bun).

The prompt 0.5.4 injected ended with a listing of OpenCode's built-in skills: `customize-opencode`, "use when editing opencode's own configuration … agents, plugins, MCP servers". On 2026-10-25 a model asked to register an MCP server read exactly that and called the official `skill` tool for the name, twice; the host happened to carry a `skill` tool of its own and answered `skill "customize-opencode" is unknown or no longer available` — the tier's error wearing the host's name. The listing was 0.5.4's own invention, not part of the proven shape: opencode2api's field-deployed prompts end at `</env>` and name no skills at all.

- The injected prompt now ends at OpenCode's environment block. No built-in skill is advertised, because a host that is not OpenCode has none of them to load; the official `skill` tool stays in the tool set, captured as-is.
- Tests pin it: the prompt is asserted to end at `</env>` and to contain no `<available_skills>`/`customize-opencode`, across the 1.x/2.x derivation and all three protocols' injection.
- The gate's default probe model moves from `minimax-m3.1-flash-free` (deprecated by the route on 2026-10-25, 410 `ModelDeprecated`) to `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, which the 410 answer itself names — a retired probe made every `check:gate` run say nothing.
- node --test 796 pass (the 8 capture tests want Bun); MAINTAINING.md gains the "advertising a skill the host does not have" entry.
